texts: In saffron robes he sits like a bridegroom in a palanquin, yet his heart is as salty as the sea and no sweetness has touched it.
doha on a guy in ochre robes carried around in a palanquin by followers, but still as salty and bitter inside
The swami in our town travels in a decorated palanquin, preaching renunciation, and then gets angry when his tea has too little salt. What would Kabir say?

Lines about a man who wears saffron robes and rides in a palanquin on the shoulders of devotees, calling himself a renunciant, though his mind still craves salt and spice and every pleasure of the world.
ochre robe, palanquin, salt
doha about shaving your head but keeping the same mind
The head is shaved bald as a polished bowl, but the thoughts remain tangled like the hair that was cut.
My brother shaved his head and moved into an ashram last year, but he still gets jealous of every cousin who gets a promotion. Can you write something for him?
I want a Kabir style doha for the one who shaves his head, puts on ochre robes, and goes out into the world proclaiming his renunciation, though the old desires still live untouched inside his mind.
shaved head, same mind
ochre robes, cuckoo, gold

A man in saffron robes came to our village collecting gold for his holy mission, and he sang so sweetly, like a cuckoo, that nobody noticed he was staring at the jewelry. Could you write a doha on that?
A couplet for the holy robed man with the sweet voice of a cuckoo who preaches that the world is an illusion, while his eyes shine and his fingers curl at the sight of gold.
doha: cuckoo sings sweet but this holy man in robes only cares about gold
The cuckoo's song is honest; the saffron robe hides a hand reaching for gold.
sacred thread, sword, show
There was this man at the protest, wearing a long thread across his chest and holding a sword, shouting about faith, and he looked ready to hurt someone. Kabir doha?
doha about a man in robes with a sacred thread and a sword, looks holy, acts violent
Compose a doha on the one who wears the robes and the sacred thread of the faithful, yet carries a sword in his hand and murder in his heart, mistaking the outer dress for the inner truth.
The thread across his chest is white as new snow, the sword in his hand is red as dawn.
ochre robes, unchanged
doha about people dressing as saints without being saints
Write about the one who dons the orange robe of renunciation, grows out his hair into matted tresses, and wanders from town to town earning respect, though his mind runs after the same old cravings.
Dyed cloth does not dye the soul; the mind should be coloured, not the robe.
My neighbour started wearing ochre robes after his business failed. He tells everyone he's a renunciant now, but he still follows stock prices on his phone. A doha?
doha: peacock feathers on his crown but a bitter gourd mind
He wears the peacock's feathers on his head, and the bitter gourd of his temper in his heart.
peacock feathers, bitter gourd

A Kabir style doha about the man who adorns himself in peacock feathers and robes of saffron, looking like a divine being, yet his heart is as bitter as the gourd, however many holy waters he washes in.
At the festival, a man in a peacock feather crown posed for photos, then yelled at the vendor for giving him a bitter gourd. A doha for him?
doha: the rainbird calls for one drop, but the robed man just wants attention
The man in saffron at our gathering says he longs for God like the rainbird for rain, but he checks how many people are filming him. Doha please
Compose a verse on the rainbird who truly yearns for a single drop and the man in ochre robes who only plays at yearning, his matted hair and robes a costume of longing without the real thirst.
rainbird, ochre robe
The rainbird thirsts without a costume; the one in ochre robes thirsts only for applause.
Matted hair, bare chest, a rough begging bowl: the mind is dressed in much finer garments of pride.
matted hair, unmoved
write a doha on the guys with matted hair and long beards who think it makes them spiritual
Write me a doha about the man who lets his hair grow into matted tresses and his beard to his chest and sits by the roadside collecting alms, though a greedy, restless mind still rules every thought.
My cousin grew out his hair and beard after reading a book on renunciation and now lectures everyone, but he still lives on his parents' money. A doha?
After my uncle's retirement he put on ochre robes and began giving advice to the whole family, but he still won't pay for anything and complains about every bill. Doha about him?
He changed his robes the way a cobra changes skin, and the poison was never shed.
robes, ego
doha about changing clothes like a monk but not changing inside

Please write a couplet for those who change their dress, their hair and their name and say they have left the world, though they have only changed what the eyes can see, and the mind remains the same.
doha about a robed man begging at the crossroads while his heart is just as greedy
The man in saffron at the crossroads near our office blesses every passerby and swears at the ones who don't give money. Please write something for him.
A doha on the one in ochre robes who stands at the crossroads asking each passerby for alms and blessing only those who give, a renunciant in dress with the hunger of a merchant in his heart.
At the crossroads he stands in sacred dress, blessing the generous, cursing the rest.
crossroads, ochre robes
About the oil press crushing mustard day and night, and the man in ochre robes who sits near it blessing the owner for a share of the oil, a renunciant who has kept every attachment of the world.
The oil press turns without a word; the robed one turns the talk, and takes a share of the oil.
doha: oil press owner supports a robe wearing man who just wants free oil
The oil press owner near us gives free oil every week to a man in saffron who says he has renounced everything. I think the man has not renounced even his hunger. Doha for this?
oil press, saffron robes

A doha about the spinning wheel that turns out honest work and the rainbird calling for truth, against the man in saffron robes who dresses as a renunciant but has no true thirst, only the pose of one.

My grandmother still uses her spinning wheel every morning and says it is her prayer; the man in saffron robes next to us talks of yearning like a rainbird but never did one day of honest work. A doha?
doha: spinning wheel, rainbird, saffron robes, you know hypocrisy
spinning wheel, rainbird, costume
The spinning wheel turns in honest hands; the rainbird calls without disguise; the robes alone stay silent.
Gold lies hidden beneath the ochre robe as the fish hides in the water, and only the hook of truth will bring it up.
gold, fish, ochre robes

Write about the man who wears ochre robes and speaks like a renunciant but lures the foolish like a fisherman luring fish, collecting gold from the faithful while claiming to have renounced it altogether.
The self-styled holy man who came to our town square with his robes and sweet talk caught a lot of fish, I mean followers, and took their gold. I felt sick. Doha for that?
doha about gold and fish and the robe wearing man baiting people
doha: a robed man smells of musk like a musk deer and eats jaggery sweets, still claims renunciation
musk deer, jaggery, saffron robes
The musk deer runs after the fragrance within it, and the robed man after the jaggery he swore to give up.
My neighbour, who dresses in saffron and says he has renounced pleasure, loves jaggery sweets and chases a different scent each day like a musk deer. Doha for him?

A verse about the man in saffron robes who preaches renunciation yet eats jaggery sweets and perfumes himself with musk, like the musk deer which races through the wilds hunting for a scent it carries within.
priest, arrow, robes
The priest in our lane wears bright robes and a long beard and speaks of non violence, but he talks about taking aim at his rivals like an arrow. Can you write a doha on that?
The priest in his fine robes shoots words like arrows, the robe unchanged, the mind unmoved.
doha: priest in fancy robes shooting arrows with his words

Write a couplet for the priest who dresses in flowing robes and speaks softly of peace and compassion, yet each word he utters is an arrow fired at some rival, and his heart has not changed since youth.
The winnowing fan lets the husk of dress blow off in the wind, and the tortoise of the true self remains within its shell.

A doha on how the winnowing fan separates grain from chaff, and how a tortoise draws itself into its shell, while the one in ochre robes pretends to have withdrawn from the world but has only changed his dress.
My uncle in orange robes says he has withdrawn from the world like a tortoise, but he still sorts every argument at home like a winnowing fan sorts grain, watching TV news all day. Doha idea?
doha: tortoise pulling in, winnowing fan, robed man who's still attached
winnowing fan, tortoise, robes
Write a doha about the groom in a palanquin dressed as a holy man at a play, and the churn that turns the curd honestly in the kitchen, asking who is closer to truth, the costume or the work.
At the wedding, the groom was carried in a palanquin dressed in saffron like a renunciant for fun, and my grandmother at the churn laughed. She said he looked holier than the real ones. Doha?
palanquin, churn, saffron robes
doha: palanquin man in robes vs the churn lady working honestly
Carried in a palanquin in robes of renunciation, he is a king of show; the woman at the churn is a queen of truth.
The blind man in ochre robes leads the blind, weighing nothing on the scales but the cloth on his back.
Write a doha about the blind man who wears the robes of a wise seer and the scales that weigh his deeds, in which the cloth weighs heavy but the heart does not weigh anything at all.
A blind man in a saffron robe was declared a wise seer by the town, and the scales of the grocer were checked and found false, as was he. Could you write a doha on that?
blind man, scales, robes
doha: blind man in saffron robes leading others, scales weigh him as light
rainbird, moth, ochre robes
Compose a doha about the rainbird which calls only for one drop, the moth which burns for the light, and the man in ochre robes who has neither the thirst nor the burning, only the costume of both.
doha: rainbird thirsts, moth burns, saffron guy just poses
My friend wears long saffron robes to every event and talks about love for God, but he has never lost sleep over anything, unlike the moth that burns or the rainbird that cries. A doha?
The rainbird cries, the moth burns, the one in ochre robes only poses for the world.
doha: a bee goes to every flower, a one-string lute man in robes goes to every rich home
bee, one-string lute, robes
A verse on the bee that visits each flower for honey, honest in its work, and the singer in ochre robes with his one-string lute who visits each rich home and sings for the sweets of donation.
The singer in saffron robes plays a one-string lute at weddings and eats from every plate like a bee at a flower, then tells us all to give up desire. Doha on him?
The bee seeks honey in blooms, the robed singer with his one-string lute seeks it in the pockets of the rich.

Write a doha on the man in ochre robes whose forehead shines with sandalwood paste and who claims to have found the paras, the alchemist's touch, though it is only a trick of clothing and pride, not a real miracle.
sandalwood, paras, robes
Sandalwood on his skin and robes upon his back, he claims the paras, the alchemist's touch, but only owns its story.
A man in saffron came to my cousin's place with sandalwood perfume saying he held the paras, the alchemist's touch, and could multiply his savings. He took the savings and vanished. Doha?
doha about robes and sandalwood and a guy claiming he found the paras, the alchemist's touch
He took off his coat and wore a robe, but who can take off the mind?
After he lost his job, my friend put on ochre robes, grew his beard, and took a new name, but he is still angry at his old boss. Could you write a doha for him?
doha: changing clothes doesn't change the person, saffron edition
new robes, old mind
Write a Kabir style doha for those who take off their ordinary clothes and put on the orange robe, take up a new name and a new voice, but leave the same old mind to wander its familiar path.
A doha about the one in saffron robes who preaches renunciation yet drinks milk from silver cups and plays a one-string lute for the audience, a holy man in costume with the appetites of a king.
doha: milk and a one-string lute and robes, lol the renunciant lifestyle
milk, one-string lute, robes
The robed singer who came to our home asked for fresh milk, three sweets and a bigger fee before he would play his one-string lute for us. Could you write a doha about this?
He sings of renunciation on a one-string lute but drinks his milk from silver.
About the yogi who has smeared his body with dust, wears matted hair and a loincloth, and sits at the roadside, but whose mind wanders to wealth, praise and the comforts of the world he gave up.
The yogi's matted tresses reach the ground, yet his thoughts have not touched the earth.
yogi, matted hair, unchanged
A yogi lived near our school with matted hair and a loincloth, and on Sundays he would be seen secretly buying sweets. We kids found it funny. Doha on him?
doha: yogi with matted hair but still full of cravings
My school friend is now a famous orator in orange robes but cannot speak to his own father. What would Kabir say?
Compose a verse for the man who has taken to the robe, shaved his head and left his family, boasting of his freedom, though his mind drags every old chain behind it wherever he goes.
robes, old chains
He has left behind the village, but not the villager within him.
doha about people who put on robes and still carry all their baggage
swan, dew, robes
The swan in its white feathers drinks no dew for show; the robed man's whiteness is only in his cloth.
A doha about the swan, pure by nature and not by dress, which separates cream from water, and the one in white or ochre robes who is not pure inside though he is dewy eyed in public.
The man who leads our weekly sermon dresses all in white like a swan and cries real dew drops at every story, but treats his driver terribly. Doha idea?
doha: swan, dew, white robes, outwardly pure only
heron, robes
A doha about the heron that stands as still as a saint in white, with the look of deep meditation, while the man in ochre robes copies the same stillness and the same hunger in his heart.
The man at the lake wears bright robes and stands for hours in a pose of meditation and my friend says he looks exactly like a heron waiting for his meal. Doha for that?
doha: heron in white robes pose, saint who isn't
The heron wears white and stands as still as a sage; the hunger behind his eyes is only for his catch.
Write a doha that says the saffron colour or the shaven head does not make a person holy, because holiness is not in the hair or the dress but in the clear, quiet mind, which no tailor can stitch.
No tailor can stitch a quiet mind, no barber can shave away desire.
haircut, no holiness
write a doha: you can't get holy just from a haircut and robes
My father shaved his head for a vow and now acts superior to all of us because he is 'on the path'. Could you write a doha for the family?
At the funeral the family reciter wore spotless white robes and a shroud-like shawl and cried loudly, but he was asking about his fee within the hour. Doha for this please
doha: wearing a shroud like robe doesn't make you detached
shroud, robes, show
He wraps himself in a shroud of white, as though dead to the world, but the world is alive in his thoughts.
Write a doha about the one who dresses in plain white like a shroud and claims he is dead to the world and its pleasures, but whose mind lives busily in every desire the world can offer.
doha: an inn full of robed men, moths around the glow of fame
inn, moth, saffron robes
In the inn the saffron-robed gather around the glow of praise like moths, and burn only their pride.
A doha about the roadside inn where robed men gather to share stories of their renunciation, the very men who circle the glow of praise like a moth, and whose renunciation burns up only in that glow.
In the inn on our highway, a group of robed men fought over a free meal while preaching about giving up desire. A moth fluttering by seemed more detached. Can you write a doha?
doha: diamond rings on a robed man in the forest, hypocrisy
Within the forest he sits in rough robes, a diamond hidden in his bag, and his austerity is only theatre.
diamond, forest, robes
Write about the man who retires to the forest in robes of austerity, takes up a hermit's pose, and keeps a diamond hidden in his bag, because he has left the town but not his love of wealth.
A man in ochre robes retired to a hut in the forest near us, and we found out he kept a diamond ring from his wife and checks its price every week. A doha?
doha: bee and tortoise vs man in robes pretending to withdraw
bee, tortoise, robes
A doha about the tortoise which draws into its shell, the bee which gathers honey from each flower, and the man in robes who claims the first but secretly lives the second in every home he visits.
The tortoise withdraws, the bee drinks honey; the one in robes does neither, but wears the look of both.
A neighbour in saffron robes said he withdrew from the world like a tortoise and yet buzzed around every home like a bee for free sweets. A doha, please?
At the crossroads the crow in a black robe caws holy words; the crowd takes him for a sage.
A doha about the crow at the crossroads who dresses himself in dark robes and calls out sacred words, fooling every passerby into thinking he is wise, while he is only waiting for crumbs of charity.
doha about a crow type fake holy man sitting at the crossroads
The man in robes who sits at the crossroads near my office caws out holy phrases like a crow all day, and when I walk past, he looks at my lunch bag. Kabir would laugh. Doha?
crossroads, crow, robes

Write a doha on those who proudly wear marks of rank on their dress and bodies, the robes of the order and the clean shaven head, believing these will carry them to freedom while the mind stays chained.
What use are saffron and shaved head if the chain of the mind is still tied?
My nephew just joined an order and posts pictures of his new robes every day. He seems happier about the robes than about the study. A doha for him?
doha about proudly wearing the uniform of holiness
robes, order, illusion
My uncle's guru wears orange robes and travels in an expensive car, and when I asked about it he said the car is also God's will. A doha for that?

Compose a doha on the teacher in orange robes who lectures against comfort and possessions but rides in a costly car, sleeps on soft beds and expects the finest meals from his followers wherever he goes.
He teaches that comfort is chains, then rests his head on silk.
doha: robes and luxury cars, kabir would have something to say
robes, luxury
What good the long beard, the shaven head, the dyed robe, if the mind is not dyed in the Name?
Write a Kabir style doha on a man who has grown a long beard, shaved his head, and dyed his robes in saffron and ochre, and who believes that these outward changes are all it takes to be holy.
doha: beard, shaved head, robe, mind is the same, classic kabir
beard, head, robes
Everyone in my office says our new colleague looks like a saint with his beard and saffron scarf, but he is the biggest gossip in the building. Could you write a doha?

Write a doha about the oil press that squeezes mustard, and the singer in robes with his one-string lute, who tells the villagers to leave all desires, then returns every evening to eat his share of the oil.
The oil press grinds and the one-string lute sings; the robed man eats from both.
The singer who came to our village plays a one-string lute for coins and also asks the oil press owner for free oil, all while wearing saffron and speaking of renunciation. A doha?
doha: one-string lute and oil press, a robed man gets fed by both
one-string lute, oil press, robes
Fish in the stream do not need robes to be holy; the man by the bank in ochre robes catches them and calls it sacrifice.
The man in saffron who sits by our pond with a fishing rod says he has renounced the world, but he sells every fish he catches. A doha on him?

A verse about a fisherman who wears the robes of renunciation and says he has left the world, yet sits on the bank every day trying to catch a fish, caught in the very desire he swore he had renounced.
doha: robe wearing guy fishing and saying he's detached
fish, robes, desire
doha: blind man in a robe pretending to see the truth

Write a doha about the blind man in saffron robes, led by his followers and claiming to see truth that others cannot, though his own eyes are closed, so that the blind leading the blind both fall into the pit.
blind man, robes
A blind man in orange robes was brought to our village and the villagers believed he could see the future, so they gave him all their savings. He couldn't even see the cheating cook. A doha?
Blind in both eyes, he wears the robe of a seer; the sighted follow, and all fall together.
doha: dew on robes in the morning, changes nothing inside
dew, robes
One cold morning I saw a man in orange robes standing in the dew, shivering and posing for his followers' phones. It was obviously staged. Can you write a doha about it?
Dew wets the saffron robe at dawn, and by noon it is gone; so too the show of renunciation.

A doha about the morning dew that clings to the robes of the holy man for a moment before the daylight dries it, much like his renunciation, which glistens in public and vanishes before the day is half over.

Write a couplet on how a person may wear the finest robe of renunciation, shave the head, and give up ordinary clothes, but the mind remains the same until it is truly purified in the heart and turned toward truth.
robes, unchanged mind
doha idea: clothes don't change the mind
My friend wore orange robes and went off to the hills for a year, and when he came back, he still argues about the same old things. Is there a doha on that?
He changed the colour of the cloth but not the colour of his thoughts.
The singer at our colony wears saffron robes and plays a one-string lute, and he rushes off whenever the fire alarm goes, so scared of fire for someone who says he is detached from life. Doha?
Compose a doha on the one in ochre robes who tends a sacred fire and plays a one-string lute, speaking of the world's illusions, but runs away at the first small fire in the neighbour's yard.
one-string lute, fire, robes
doha: fire and one-string lute and robes, fake renunciation
He sings of the burning world on his one-string lute, yet leaps from the fire to save his skin.
doha about robe wearing people who catch followers in a net
net, saffron robes
The net is cast in saffron cloth, and the simple believers swim into it of their own accord.
A verse on the man who spreads his net of sweet speech and ochre robes over the village, catching the simple and the faithful, who think they are being rescued when they are being caught.
After the man in robes came to our colony, half the people gave him their savings, caught in a net of promises. Can you make this into a doha?
Write a doha on the rainbird, which wears no costume and cries for one drop out of true longing, in contrast with the man in robes who wears the garb of longing but has never really been thirsty.
The rainbird has no robe, yet its cry reaches the sky; the man in robes cries louder and no one is moved.
rainbird, fake longing
doha: robes vs rainbird honest longing
My uncle puts on ochre robes for every festival to look holy, though he is a card player the rest of the year. I think the rainbird has more faith. Doha?
Compose a verse about those who think that matted hair, a body smeared with dust and a staff in the hand can make a man holy, while the mind inside runs wild like an untamed beast.
doha about thinking you're holy because of how you look
My cousin's new boyfriend wears all the holy symbols and robes, and then breaks every promise he makes. She asked me if I could find a doha for it
Appearance is a robe that any can wear; character is one that must be woven.
appearance, not holiness
He wore the ochre robes at the ceremony, spoke the great words about giving up the world, and was seen later bargaining fiercely over a plot of land. A doha, please
Write a doha for those who can speak eloquently about renouncing the world in their robes and then argue fiercely over a small piece of land, for the dress changed but the desires did not.
robes, land quarrel
doha: robes, but fighting over land lol
Robes of renunciation on the shoulder, a title deed in the pocket.
Our village's holy man in ochre robes was caught drinking from the well at night and cursing the neighbours who saw him. Kabir doha for this?
doha about a robe wearing man at the well, fake renunciation
He wears the robe at the well in daylight and the thirst of the world in his heart at night.
well, ochre robes
A doha on the man in ochre robes who lectures at the village well about letting go of desires, but is first in the queue to fill his own vessel and shouts at anyone who gets there before him.
doha: traveler in a monk's robe who is just a tourist
The traveler in saffron wanders from town to town, and carries the same worries in his bag.
A verse about the traveler who puts on robes and sets out to wander the world, believing the journey itself makes him holy, but who brings along his old pride and greed in his pack.
A traveler in orange robes stayed at our home for three days, talked about leaving everything behind, and then asked us to wash and press his robes and cook him special food. Doha?
traveler, robes, ego
My uncle's guru wears a plain cloth sheet around him as a sign of poverty, but the cage of his ego is gilded and he lives in a luxury ashram. A doha on this?
A plain cloth sheet around the body, a golden cage around the self.
doha: cloth sheet and cage, simple dress but locked-in mind
Write a doha on the one who covers himself in a simple cloth sheet to show his poverty, while remaining locked in the cage of his own pride, a bird who sings of freedom behind golden bars.
cloth sheet, cage, show
Prayer beads at the neck, a shadow of pride at his feet: the garb is perfect, the heart unchanged.
doha: prayer beads and robes, even the shadow looks fake
The man at the bus stop wears prayer beads and saffron robes, and his shadow looked so proud on the pavement that I laughed. A doha?
prayer beads, shadow, robes

Write a doha on the man who wears prayer beads and saffron robes everywhere, yet follows his own shadow of ego, which stretches long behind him and which no clothing, however holy, can ever make shorter.
